tested_commit: recorded in the pull request body with its CI run ids
evidence_class: Signed fixture launch grants from LaunchAuthority, fakeredis, fixture server clock and a SQLite fixture ledger; served over a loopback HTTP server in tests; no live rollout. Live G3 qualification is separate.
interfaces: GET /v2/tasks/<task>: the credential's own task, its execution relevant fields and a revision digest over them; another task is forbidden_scope with no detail about it

PATCH /v2/tasks/<task>: worker fields only (state claimed, blocked or pr; issue, pull request, branch and its repository), guarded by expected_revision inside the ledger write; a stale revision is revision_conflict with the current revision and counts in ledger_revision_conflicts_total

POST /v2/tasks/<task>/progress and POST /v2/tasks/<task>/comments: aliases writing the same task comment thread with the same receipt, so a progress line and a comment with one operation_id and text replay each other; idempotent per operation_id, need no revision, so progress survives a specification edit; the same id with other content is operation_conflict

POST /v2/tasks/<task>/outcomes: an outcome proposal (done or blocked, with proof) guarded by expected_revision and idempotent per operation_id; it is written as a task comment and never sets done, which stays the operator's
/v2/swarm/*: swarm controls refuse worker credentials with forbidden_scope
scripts.swarm_v2.api.server.Routes and serve: one loopback HTTP server carries the execution endpoints and the task endpoints
TasksAPI(writes_enabled=False): the rollback read only mode

supported_versions.python: 3.11 and 3.12 unit shards in the linked CI run
supported_versions.protocol: SV2-LDG-02 launch grants, registrations and task generations; stale generations answer stale_generation
supported_versions.ledger: The SQLite ledger repository through apply_ops with a gate; the ledger stays the single writer of task state
supported_versions.compatibility: The local ledger server and its operator writes are unchanged; the v2 endpoints are additive

states.observed: The task row and its specification revision read from the ledger
states.accepted: A request whose credential, task generation, claim and expected revision hold at the gate
states.committed: The ledger write inside apply_ops, with its receipt stored in the ledger metadata in the same commit
states.externally_verified: None; no production deployment and no live rollout yet

authoritative_objects: The ledger document and its task rows and comments are authoritative operator work state and are never deleted as caches; the task_operations receipts in the ledger metadata are an idempotency cache for the current task generation only: a new generation's first write replaces them, which is safe because the claim check refuses every write from a superseded generation before any receipt is consulted
The Redis task claims and launch registrations from SV2-LDG-02 are authoritative for who may write
The ledger-revision-conflicts counter is a measurement, not state

rollback_rehearsal.action: Construct TasksAPI with writes_enabled=False: reads still answer and every write gets a read only revision_conflict naming the current revision. The revision is a digest computed on read from the stored specification fields, so rollback removes no stored metadata
rollback_rehearsal.data_safety: The ledger document is byte equal before and after the refused writes; nothing is deleted

remaining_limitations: No production process starts the v2 HTTP server yet, for the execution endpoints or the task endpoints, so the read only switch is a constructor flag with no operator control until a deployment package adds one
The window between the Redis claim check and the SQLite commit is owned by SV2-LDG-04
Receipts for the current task generation grow with each operation, uncapped
Routes matches the raw request path, so a query string on a task path answers 404, the same as the execution endpoints

decisions: An outcome proposal requires expected_revision although it writes only a comment: done or blocked is a claim about the task measured against its specification, so a proposal made against an older specification is stale work and is refused like a stale update
Paused writes answer revision_conflict with read_only true and are not counted in ledger_revision_conflicts_total, because a pause is not a specification conflict
